brief: CTAs are riding this week's equity rally without having driven it. Last week's model showed limited incremental CTA buying under most upside scenarios. Nasdaq-100 rose 3.3% led by tech after META's Muse launch reignited AI enthusiasm. Trend followers are long S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures across all model speeds and could add Nasdaq-100 length next week as bullish signals strengthen, while Russell 2000 stays vulnerable to further CTA selling on continued small-cap underperformance. Trend followers remain stretched short US Treasuries as yields rose on strong PMI data, higher oil prices, and weak 5yr and 7yr auctions. That short stays intact unless 10yr yields fall roughly 18bp, though a Korean yield decline already stopped out some risk-averse KTB shorts. USD posted a second straight weekly gain, drawing CTA buying versus AUD and MXN on stop-outs, and could extend against every currency except JPY next week. CTAs stay long WTI crude, with the stop-loss trigger about 5.4% away, and gold trend signals keep fading. SPX hedger gamma retreated to $6.9bn (72nd percentile) from Tuesday's near-second-highest $14.1bn peak. Wednesday's month-end expiry is next week's largest gamma driver at $2.4bn.
